summary: "Escape keeps in-flight edits" test no longer exercises Escape at all — onCancel is now a no-op, so the test reduces to the already-covered commit path
claim: The test is the regression guard for exactly this change: it drives the real Escape sequence (onCancel, then the blur's onCommit) and asserts the typed text is persisted. If onCancel were made to set the `cancelled` flag again (the old discard behaviour), onCommit would skip the store write and the assertion would fail.
evidence: packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts: onCommit writes only `if (!cancelled)`; the old onCancel set `cancelled = true`, the new one is `() => {}`.

packages/slides/test/view/editor/text-box-editor.test.ts: the test calls `tb.fireCancel()` then `tb.fireCommit([paragraph('typed-then-escaped')])` and expects the stored text to be 'typed-then-escaped' — under the old code it stays 'hello' (that is what the replaced test asserted).
A plain commit test does not call fireCancel first, so it cannot catch a regression where Escape suppresses the write.

summary: Revision-preview's key suppressor deliberately lets Escape through on the premise that Escape is NON-DESTRUCTIVE in both engines — this diff makes Escape a store write in the slides/board editor
claim: Escape cannot cause a new store write while the preview is open: opening the preview moves focus to the overlay, which blurs any live slides text box, and a blur commits that edit (it always did, before and after this change). By the time Escape reaches the editor there is no text edit left, so Escape only clears a selection. The premise stands; the comment now says so.
evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/history/revision-preview.tsx: the suppressor effect first runs `rootRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true })`, moving focus out of the editor.

packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts enterEditMode: the docs text box routes its blur through onCommit, which writes unless `cancelled` — and the old code's Escape only set `cancelled`, it never made blur skip the write. So a blur-commit on opening the preview happens identically before and after this diff.
packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts documents the measured behaviour: the slides text editor 'writes back to the store on BLUR'.
The suppressor comment was updated in this branch to state this explicitly.
